Background (verified, @netlify/identity 2.0.0): browser login sets the nf_jwt cookie; getUser() reads the cookie server-side and can fall back to JWT claims when Identity is unreachable, so it is NOT proof the account still exists. Because browser auth is a cookie, CSRF protection is required: verifyRequestOrigin on every state-changing route. Never treat context.user as the Identity user.

What: auth middleware producing a principal { kind: 'user', identityId, email, confirmed } from the cookie. Live check: admin.getUser per user, cached 5 minutes, fail closed if the lookup fails; reject deleted, unconfirmed, or DB-disabled users and emails that moved outside the allowed domains. verifyRequestOrigin on POST/PATCH/DELETE for cookie principals. A bearer key and a cookie are never mixed on one request.

Done when: middleware is used by all /api/v1 routes and covered by tests: valid cookie, missing cookie, forged origin, deleted user with valid cookie, Identity outage (fail closed), changed email.

Background: anyone in the world can deploy the template, so admission must fail closed. ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS selects the mode:
- Domain mode (e.g. netlify.com): confirmed email at an allowed domain (exact match after lowercasing); Identity autoconfirm must be OFF, or people could claim addresses they don't own.
- Invite-only mode (value invite-only, a sentinel because Deploy button inputs are required): Identity registration must be set to invite only; only invited users join.
Identity's default registration is Open.

Enforced in three places:
1. netlify/functions/identity.ts with the typed userValidate handler: event.deny() for outside domains (domain mode) or every self sign-up (invite-only; va-uys.8 [S7] must confirm invite acceptance still works, else use the alternative va-uys.8 [S7] chose).
2. getSettings: until registration/autoconfirm match the mode, every endpoint except setup/health returns setup_required.
3. When creating a user's DB row: domain mode needs a confirmed email at an allowed domain; invite-only needs an invite-created, confirmed account. Accounts created while settings were wrong are not admitted.

Done when: tests cover both modes, misconfigured settings, outside domains, case-folding, and accounts created under wrong settings.

title: Remix a video: a new video from another video's composition plus a change request
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: remix a video (a new video that starts from another video's finished composition plus a change request). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-03-remix.md (draft 3, commit 73bea33; §0 = owner decisions from the 2026-11-03 interview, §10 = review log of the Fable 5.1 + Codex gpt-6.1-sol reviews). Line refs are as of 73bea33.
Spec key: RM
Spec section(s): all (§0-§9)

## Background
Owner ask (2026-11-03): from a video, press Remix, say what should change, and get a NEW video that starts from the
original's finished composition, prompts and settings rather than from scratch: a clone plus a revision. People will use
it every way, from "exactly this, swap the brand names" to "a video like this about a totally different topic".

What already exists (spec §1): every finished version keeps its whole composition as sources/{jobId}/v{n}.tar.gz
(index.html, summary.json, agent-made assets, AI voice clips, music credits; <=10 MiB tar limit; hash in
outputs.sha256, finalize.ts:217), library media as version_media snapshots (key + hash), and its settings on the
versions row. Revisions already restore a parent archive into video/ and ask the agent to change it
(reviseVideo videos.ts:369-464, reconciler.ts:252-277, prepare-run.ts:376-395). A remix is that run with three
differences: the parent is in another video, the result is a new video owned by the remixer, and some state is dropped
(recorded narration, edit state, captions).

Owner decisions (§0): no fidelity toggle (the agent infers how much to change); entry points on the video page, a Library
tile menu, the public share page (signed-in Creators only) and New video ("Start from an existing video" search picker);
optional Plan first like revisions; immediate-source lineage only; apply today's brand; source media as removable
chips; source length prefilled; language inherited (transcription only); no owner opt-out; admin kill switch
remixEnabled (on by default); empty "What would you change?" box; source comments not carried; "Remix" in the Library
meta line, no filter; no owner notification; aspect change allowed with a warning; recorded narration dropped
deterministically; no remix counts on the original.

## Approach
Phases: 1 data + run path; 2 remixVideo domain (copy, clean, adopt, create) + plans; 3 API, MCP, config, OpenAPI, mock;
4 UI (dialog, four entry points, admin toggle); 5 production e2e + docs. Each phase ends with a gate bead; gates chain.

Architecture (spec §3): at creation, copy the source archive to sources/{newJobId}/remix-source.tar.gz under a narrow
reservation cleanup row (+1 h) that the creating transaction adopts (marks done); clean recorded narration out of the
copy with applyNarration(…, null); snapshot everything a run needs in versions.remix so retries never read the
original. Runs reuse the existing `revision` kind: the reconciler builds manifest.source from versions.remix
(parentN null, no references). Provenance on jobs.remix_of_job_id/_n (immediate source).

## Done when
Every phase epic closed; the phase 5 live gate passed on production; CI green; the spec gets a short as-built note
(deviations, credits spent).

## Tests
Each phase has a gate bead; unit/integration/UI tests are listed per bead.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

## Considerations
Not in v1 (spec §8): remix counts/reverse links on the original, a Remixes filter, stored lineage chains, owner
notifications, owner opt-out, keeping recorded narration, translation semantics for the language field, picking source
comments, multi-source remixes, streaming blob copies. A separate follow-up (dismissible comments in Incorporate
feedback, spec §9) is NOT part of this epic. Production e2e spends credits (budget ~600 for phase 5).
close_reason: Remix shipped: 81f29f2, f140741, b9476b7, 975a1ae; live on production; gate passed with vid_01m6jjjerhj59402m1mqzp9a8g

description:

Line refs are as of 73bea33.
Spec key: 2.2
Spec section(s): §2 gotchas 2 and 7, §3.1 steps 2-6

## Background
The remix must own a copy of its source so it survives the original's deletion (deleteVideo queues delete_prefix for
{jobId}/ in videos, sources, bundles, videos.ts:640-649) and so run checks stay per-job. Two traps (verified): the
sweep deletes ANY due row's prefix with no existence check (cleanup.ts:29-32), and insertCleanup is onConflictDoNothing
on unique (store, prefix) (drizzle.ts:1192), so a row for {newJobId}/ would either delete a successful remix or later
swallow deleteVideo's own row and leak the remix's files. BlobsPort has only buffered get/set (deps.ts:142-152).

## Approach
src/domain/remix-copy.ts (used by remixVideo, bead 2.3):
1. reserve(repo, newJobId): insertCleanup({ kind: 'delete_prefix', store: 'sources', prefix: `${newJobId}/remix-source`,
   nextActionAt: now + 1 h }) -> returns the row id. The narrow prefix never collides with deleteVideo's `${newJobId}/`.
2. copy(deps, source output, cleaned bytes): blobs.set('sources', `${newJobId}/remix-source.tar.gz`, bytes); read back
   and verify sha256 (strong consistency store).
3. adopt(repo, reservationId) inside the creating transaction: updateCleanup(id, { doneAt: now }). listDueCleanup only
   takes doneAt null rows (drizzle.ts:1198), so an adopted copy is never swept.
Failure anywhere after reserve (exception, tx rollback, lost idempotency race, crash) leaves the row open; the sweep
deletes the orphan copy within the hour.

## Done when
The three helpers exist, are used by remixVideo, and the lifecycle is covered by tests (most in 2.5).

## Tests
- Unit: reserve row shape; copy verifies hash (a fake blobs store that corrupts on read fails the copy); adopt sets doneAt.
- deleteVideo on an adopted remix still inserts and runs its own {jobId}/ cleanup (no conflict with the reservation row)
  and the copy is gone afterwards.

   (409 not_ready otherwise). Visibility BEFORE the idempotency lookup, like reviseVideo (videos.ts:391-392), so a key
   can't replay a remix of a video you can no longer see.
3. withIdempotency scope `videos.remix:${sourceId}` (so one key used on two sources conflicts rather than replays).
4. newJobId; reserve (2.2); read output.sha256['source.tar.gz'] archive, verify; narrated = version.narration !== null
   || output.sha256['references.json'] present; cleanRemixSource (2.1; its size/validation errors become
   ApiError invalid_request "This version is too large or damaged to remix."); copy (2.2).

   still equal to deriveTitle(v1.prompt), finalize.ts:483), aspect (input ?? source), language (input ?? source),
   private: source.private, remixOfJobId, remixOfN, owner = principal }; access mirror for private videos like
   updateVideo (videos.ts:605-613, files.ts:88); v1 { prompt, authorId/apiKeyId = principal, mode 'author', parentN null,
   targetDurationSec (input ?? source), sound (input ?? source), voiceover (input ?? source), webhookUrl = input's
   only (the source's is NOT copied),
   plan/frozen/editedFromN/narration/captions/contract NOT copied, remix: VersionRemix snapshot (history = the source
   versions' prompts up to fromN, oldest first, PREFIXED with the source v1's own remix.history when the source is itself
   a remix, then capped to the newest 8 entries / 4000 chars; fromSummary = output.agentSummary capped
   1000; fromTitle; fromOwnerName; narrationDropped; sourceSound) }; version_media: when mediaIds given it REPLACES the
   set (new ids must be live library items; ids that were in the source set keep their inherited snapshot even if
   since soft-deleted, media.ts:395), else inherit the source set via snapshotMedia (media.ts:388-421); plan consume
   (bead 2.4); attempt (queued); idempotency record; adopt reservation.

title: Share page: Remix link for signed-in Creators (va_creator hint cookie + /me check)
description:

Line refs are as of 73bea33.
Spec key: 4.5
Spec section(s): §2 gotcha 10, §3.7 Public share page

## Background
/v/{slug} is rendered by netlify/edge-functions/public.ts, which has no database access and serves the same HTML to
everyone. Both sign-in methods use same-origin cookies (Identity nf_jwt, ui/src/auth.tsx:1; Sign in with Netlify
va_session, src/auth/sessions.ts:12), so a same-origin fetch('/api/v1/me', { credentials: 'same-origin' }) identifies a
signed-in teammate. Public share pages can get heavy traffic: outsiders must cause no API calls.

## Approach
- App: when a signed-in user whose role can create loads the app and config.remixEnabled, set a NON-secret cookie
  va_creator=1 (Path=/, SameSite=Lax, ~30 days, not HttpOnly; never used for authorization); clear it on sign-out and
  when the role can no longer create.
- Share page: one small inline script (respect any CSP/permissions headers public.ts sets, denyMicrophone): if
  document.cookie has va_creator=1, fetch /api/v1/me and /api/v1/config; if the user can create and remixEnabled, reveal
  a hidden "Remix in Video Agent" link to /videos/{jobId}?remix={n}. The jobId/n come from the publication mirror the edge function
  already reads (internal store pub/{slug}.json has jobId and versionN, public.ts:50-57).
- Page stays cacheable/identical for everyone.

## Done when
Signed-out visitors: no link, no /me request. Signed-in Creator: link appears and opens the dialog via 4.1's deep link. Reviewer/Viewer: no link.

## Tests
- test/edge.ts loadEdge('public'): HTML contains the hidden link + script; no per-user content.
- Playwright (mock or a local edge harness): without the cookie no request to /api/v1/me (route interception asserts
  zero calls); with cookie + creator -> link visible; with cookie + viewer -> hidden.
- Unit: cookie set/cleared on role change and sign-out.

## Background
Existing e2e scripts (scripts/e2e/*.ts with lib.ts) run against VIDEO_AGENT_URL with API keys, log JSON steps, and support --dry.

## Approach
VIDEO_AGENT_URL + VIDEO_AGENT_KEY (Creator) [+ SOURCE_ID, NARRATED_ID]. Steps, each logged:

   source's (perceptual hash close) and check the new name appears in captions/summary.
2. New-topic remix ("same format, about webhooks"): wait ready; captions differ substantially; aspect and duration

title: Phase 0: spikes that settle the unknowns
description:
Spec key: E0

Project: video-agent (repo netlify-labs/video-agent, private until open-sourced). An open-source TEMPLATE any Netlify user can deploy into their own account to get a prompt-to-MP4 video agent for their company. One repo, one Netlify project. Each video version is produced by a Netlify Agent Runner run on that same project, using HyperFrames (HTML/CSS/GSAP -> deterministic MP4) with FFmpeg/Chrome installed by netlify-agent-kit. Service = Hono+OpenAPI API in one Netlify Function, Netlify Database (Postgres via Drizzle) for records, Netlify Blobs for bytes, Netlify Identity for sign-in, React+Mantine+Vite web app, all TypeScript. Our own deployment: our internal project, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=netlify.com.

Why: several load-bearing behaviours of the platform can't be settled by reading docs or by review (two Fable+Codex review rounds already happened). Phase 0 runs small, real experiments and writes SPIKES.md. Nothing in phases 1-3 should be built on an assumption a spike is meant to test.

Unknowns: can agent runs write Blobs (and how big); does seeking a 20-100 MB MP4 streamed from Blobs through an edge function work; can previews be kept from serving production data; how Netlify Identity behaves inside a Hono catch-all Function and edge functions; whether the SDK reconciles ambiguous starts; what the Deploy button really does; how good from-scratch videos are and how long they can be.

Done when: every S-bead is closed, SPIKES.md exists, and the spec's sections 5, 6, 7, 10, 11 and 13 are updated with the results (bead va-uys.10 [S9]).

title: Spike workbench: test site, minimal template and a local run starter
description:
Spec key: S0

Background: every phase-0 spike needs (a) a Netlify site where agent runs can be started, (b) a minimal HyperFrames project in the repo so a run has something to render, and (c) a tiny local script that starts a run with a given prompt and prints the runner/session ids. The real template (va-brx.1 [W1]) and service come later; this is throwaway scaffolding on a spike branch.

What:
- Branch spike/phase-0 in netlify-labs/video-agent. A minimal video/ from `npx hyperframes init` (pinned hyperframes version), `npx netlify-agent-kit add hyperframes` so runs install FFmpeg, FFprobe, Chrome and the skills.
- Use the existing project our internal deployment or a dedicated test site; make sure Agent Runners is enabled on it and Identity is enabled (va-uys.8 [S7] needs it).
- spikes/start-run.ts (tsx): uses nax-agent-runner-sdk 0.3.0 with a PAT from env (RUNNER_API_TOKEN) to start a run from a prompt file on a given deployId or branch, wait, and print the snapshot as JSON lines. requestId must be a UUID (the SDK rejects anything else).
- spikes/README.md and an empty SPIKES.md with one section per spike (va-uys.2 [S1]-S8).

Done when: spikes/start-run.ts starts a trivial run ("print hello and finish") and logs its terminal snapshot.

Notes: nax CLI also works for ad-hoc runs (the maintainers' runner CLI run agent ... with NETLIFY_SITE_ID set to the full site id). Keep spike code out of main until W/C beads re-implement it properly.
close_reason: Workbench on spike/phase-0; hello run 45s/14 credits (SPIKES.md S0).

title: Write SPIKES.md conclusions and update the spec
description:
Spec key: S9

Background: phase 0 exists to replace assumptions with measurements before building. The spec is PLAN.md (draft 7); sections 5 (run prompt), 6 (hand-back and serving), 7 (reconciler), 10 (concurrency), 11 (auth) and 13 (deploy/setup) carry assumptions the spikes test.

What: consolidate each spike's result in SPIKES.md (table + decision + evidence links), then edit PLAN.md accordingly and record the changes in its decision log. Update downstream beads whose descriptions assumed a different outcome (br update / br comments add).

Done when: PLAN.md and the beads reflect the spike results; nothing downstream still depends on an untested assumption. Consider one more cross-model review only now, if decisions changed substantially.
close_reason: Verified (live production checks, Playwright suite, e2e PASS). Button-specific test remains under S8/U4c.

title: Spike S1: from-scratch video quality, timing, length ceiling
description:
Spec key: S1

Background: the only proven case is an agent restyling an existing 14-second HyperFrames video (99 s, 28 steps). The product needs videos made from scratch from a prompt, in four aspects (16:9 1920x1080, 9:16 1080x1920, 1:1 1080x1080, 4:5 1080x1350), with length on Auto by default (agent picks; prompt nudges 15-45 s for launch clips, tutorials longer) and no maximum length. The hard ceiling is the runner's 25-minute run limit.

What: run 6 agent runs using the spec's section-5 prompt (read context/, write video/index.html, `npx hyperframes check` to 0 errors, write video/summary.json with title, summary and caption cues, render). Vary prompts (launch clip, sales explainer, docs tutorial snippet), cover all four aspects, Auto plus targets of 15 s, 60 s and 3 min. For each, record: success, authoring time, render time, file size and render time at HyperFrames quality looks (the default, CRF 16), standard and delivery (alias of high), credits used, check retries, actual length chosen on Auto. Also compare effort medium vs the runner default on two prompts.

Score each video on a rubric: text legible at target size; requested text correct; no clipped frames; coherent narrative; acceptable motion.

Done when: SPIKES.md has the table and picks: default quality, default agent/model/effort, the authoring deadline (spec default 22 min), and the longest video length that reliably fits one run.

Notes: five or six runs are feasibility evidence, not a reliability estimate. Budget the credits; record them.
close_reason: 3 from-scratch runs, rubric pass, standard quality default (SPIKES.md S1).

title: Spike S2: private hand-back from a run (Blobs write vs signed upload) and revision round-trip
description:
Spec key: S2

Background: finished files must get from the agent run back to the service privately. Deploy previews are public and are never a fallback. Option A: the run writes the project's own Blobs (`netlify blobs:set uploads {attemptId}/video.mp4 --input ...`); it's known runners can blobs:get (the SDK's prompt offload relies on it) but blobs:set is unverified, and the CLI reads the whole file into memory. Option B: the API mints a single-use upload URL at attempt start and the script PUTs to a streaming edge function that writes to Blobs (buffered Functions cap binary bodies around 4.5 MB, so it must stream).

Revisions also depend on this: a revision run starts from the production deploy, so it has to download the parent version's sources/{jobId}/v{n}.tar.gz and restore video/ before authoring.

What:
1. From a run: blobs:set 2 MB, 20 MB and 100 MB files; an interrupted retry; list which stores/keys the runner can write.
2. A signed PUT of the same files to a throwaway streaming edge function that writes to Blobs.
3. Round-trip: run 1 makes a composition with an unmistakable change and uploads source.tar.gz; run 2 (fresh, from the pinned production deploy) downloads it with blobs:get or a signed URL, verifies the SHA-256, restores video/, revises, and the change plus referenced assets survive.

Done when: SPIKES.md says which upload path works, its size limits and retry behaviour, and confirms the revision restore path.
close_reason: Blobs write from runs works up to 100 MB; revision round-trip verified live (v2 from v1).

title: Spike S3: callback reachability and session signals at completion
description:
Spec key: S3

Background: there is no completion webhook for Agent Runner sessions (verified in @netlify/open-api 2.63.1; agent runner hooks are inbound triggers only). The service learns about completion from (1) the agent's callback POST to the production URL, (2) a sweep polling getSnapshot every minute. The callback arrives while the session is still running (the agent hasn't written its final answer yet), so it can't decide outcomes.

What: from a run, curl the project's production HTTPS URL (a throwaway function that logs the body). Capture the session's fields at completion: state (new, running, await_input, interrupted, error, done, cancelled), result, deploy_id, deploy_url, duration, steps, usage, interactions (note: there is NO preview_state). Measure the time from the callback to the terminal state.

Done when: SPIKES.md lists the finalize inputs and the callback-to-terminal latency.
close_reason: Callback reachable; receipts primary path (SPIKES.md).

title: Spike S4: edge streaming with Range for private and public files; database from edge
description:
Spec key: S4

Background: videos are served by edge functions: private files via signed URLs (/files/{jobId}/v{n}/{file}?exp=&sig=, HMAC, 10-min expiry), published files via /v/{slug}.mp4. Function responses cap at ~6 MB buffered / 20 MB streamed, so edge streaming is the plan. Blobs has no byte-range reads: a seek means skipping the stream to the offset. Edge functions have a 50 ms CPU budget and 512 MB memory. Also unknown: whether @netlify/database works inside an edge function (Deno). Edge functions need the file-signing secret (stored in a database settings row) and publication state.

What: serve 20 MB and 100 MB MP4s from Blobs through an edge function with Range in Safari and Chrome. Check 206, Content-Range, Content-Length, suffix and open-ended ranges, 416, HEAD, seek latency, memory, and upstream bytes read per seek. Expired and missing signatures must fail. Try connecting to Netlify Database from an edge function.

Done when: SPIKES.md says whether stream-skipping is good enough (else finalize stores chunked MP4s) and whether edge functions read the DB directly or a strongly-consistent Blobs mirror the API maintains.
close_reason: Signed Range delivery 206, unsigned 403, public mp4 + immediate unpublish verified live. 20/100 MB seek latency still unmeasured (noted).

title: Spike S5: nax-agent-runner-sdk inside a Netlify Function; ambiguous start reconciliation
description:
Spec key: S5

Background: the service calls nax-agent-runner-sdk 0.3.0 from Functions: start (with land: 'none', deployId, model, effort, a UUID requestId), getSnapshot, stop. The serialized handle must be saved after every mutating call. requestId is a reconciliation marker, not an exactly-once guarantee: after an ambiguous response (timeout after send) the service must find the run by requestId instead of starting a duplicate.

What: bundle the SDK in a Netlify Function; time start and getSnapshot (target p95 < 3 s); force an ambiguous start (abort after send) and reconcile by requestId; confirm the handle round-trips through serialize/deserialize.

Done when: SPIKES.md has timings and a working reconciliation recipe.
close_reason: SDK runs in Functions; queued→running 16 s live.

title: Spike S6: parallel runs, agent-run previews, and production-only deploy context
description:
Spec key: S6

Background: every agent run builds a deploy preview of the whole project, and each preview (and each agent run) gets a database branch copied from production. A preview created while a video is published would keep serving it after production unpublishes, and previews could accept jobs nothing processes. The spec's answer: every server surface (API, edge functions, callback, bootstrap) runs only on the current published production deploy (context.deploy.published + production context); elsewhere return a placeholder/404. Also: the build command should detect an agent-run build and skip the UI build.

What: start 3 runs at once (interference, platform concurrent-run ceiling). Find the env var or context that identifies an agent-run build; measure build minutes with the UI build skipped, including the preview DB branch and migrations. Publish something in production, create a preview, unpublish in production, and verify the guard makes the preview and an old deploy URL serve nothing.

Done when: SPIKES.md has the concurrency ceiling (informs MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS default 3), the agent-run detection method, the build cost, and a verified guard recipe.
close_reason: Deploy-context guard verified (permalink 404); concurrent runs fine. Agent-run UI-skip not visible in logs (noted).

title: Spike S7: Netlify Identity in a Hono catch-all Function and edge functions
description:
Spec key: S7

Background (verified from @netlify/identity 2.0.0 README): login sets the nf_jwt cookie; server-side getUser() reads that cookie (no token argument) and can fall back to JWT claims if the live lookup fails, so it is not proof the account still exists; verifyRequestOrigin is the CSRF helper; admin.getUser does a live lookup; handleAuthCallback, acceptInvite, getSettings exist. Identity's default registration is Open. New Identity event functions use typed handlers (userValidate with event.deny()). Never treat context.user as the Identity user (it's Netlify team login).

The spec's admission design: ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS = comma-separated domains (domain mode; autoconfirm must be off) or the sentinel invite-only (registration must be invite-only; userValidate denies every self sign-up).

What: in a Hono route inside one catch-all Function and in an edge function: getUser() from the cookie; verifyRequestOrigin; admin.getUser as a live check; a deleted user with a still-valid cookie; a changed email. userValidate denying an outside domain; invite-only with a deny-all userValidate AND invite acceptance still working (undocumented; critical); reading registration and autoconfirm via getSettings for /setup; handleAuthCallback for confirmation, invite and recovery links.

Done when: SPIKES.md documents the working auth recipe, and either invite acceptance passes the deny-all hook or an alternative invite-only enforcement is chosen.
close_reason: Identity sign-up, confirmation, cookie session, live check, admin bootstrap verified live.

title: Spike S8: Deploy to Netlify button from a public fixture repo
description:
Spec key: S8

Background: the Deploy button only works from a PUBLIC GitHub or GitLab repo (our repo is private until open-sourced), so the test needs a scratch public fixture with placeholder content and the real netlify.toml. [template.environment] declares required inputs with labels (blank values likely not accepted, which is why invite-only mode uses the sentinel value invite-only). USAGE.md is shown after deploy. Git-connected Agent Runners support GitHub only; Agent Runners and Netlify Database need credit-based plans with AI features.

Button variables: RUNNER_API_TOKEN (PAT for starting runs; named so the CLI isn't silently authenticated, unlike NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN), ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, ADMIN_EMAILS.

What: deploy the fixture with the button into a different team: required-input behaviour, USAGE.md, which features are on after deploy (Identity, Agent Runners, Database auto-provisioning), the PAT's permissions in the destination team, and what /setup must still check.

Done when: SPIKES.md lists the post-button checklist and any blockers for strangers. Delete the public fixture afterwards.
